articles.title: Hyderabad EON Space Labs gets patent for miniaturised space imaging system - Telangana Today
articles.content: NRI View Point cartoon My Space Reviews Education Today Property Lifestyle Home | Hyderabad | Hyderabad Eon Space Labs Gets Patent For Miniaturised Space Imaging System Hyderabad EON Space Labs gets patent for miniaturised space imaging system Hyderabad-based EON Space Labs has secured a patent for MIRA, a miniaturised space telescope-based imaging system. Weighing 502 grams, the system is designed to provide high-definition multispectral Earth observation imagery for commercial applications across agriculture, mining, marine and insurance. By Telangana Today Published Date - 29 September 2026, 03:26 PM Hyderabad: EON Space Labs, a Hyderabad-based deeptech company developing advanced electro-optical imaging systems, has been granted a patent for its miniaturised space telescope-based imaging system. MIRA is an advanced imaging system, integrated with TakeMe2Space’s MOI-1A satellite — India’s first orbital computing satellite slated for launch on board the SpaceX Transporter-18 rocket on October 1. MIRA marked its first orbital flight attempt earlier this year in January on board ISRO’s PSLV-C62 mission. While an upper-stage anomaly prevented payload deployment, the mission successfully validated MIRA’s mechanical integration, spaceflight packaging, and hardware readiness. Building on this, EON Space Labs is also accelerating its flight heritage roadmap with another upcoming orbital deployment aboard ISRO’s Small Satellite Launch Vehicle (SSLV). Codenamed MIRA, it is also certified space-grade as per NASA standards, delivering high-definition multispectral EO imagery in an ultra-compact form factor. Weighing a mere 502 grams, MIRA enables satellite operators to offer commercial EO services across agriculture, marine, mining, supply-chain management, and insurance. articles.title: India's first World Happpiness Summit concludes in Bengaluru - Telangana Today
articles.content: NRI View Point cartoon My Space Reviews Education Today Property Lifestyle Home | Lifestyle | Indias First World Happpiness Summit Concludes In Bengaluru India’s first World Happpiness Summit concludes in Bengaluru India’s first World Happpiness Summit concluded in Bengaluru, bringing together personalities from entertainment, entrepreneurship, spirituality, wellness and social leadership. The day-long event explored happiness through Pleasure, Peace and Purpose and concluded with a collective resolve to make Bengaluru the world’s happiest city. By Telangana Today Published Date - 29 September 2026, 03:02 PM Hyderabad: India’s first World Happpiness Summit concluded in Bengaluru, drawing a full-day audience into a conversation the country rarely pauses for: what does it truly take to be happy? Hosted by Happpy AiR – Atman in Ravi, the Happpiness Ambassador, the summit brought together voices from entertainment, public life, entrepreneurship, spirituality, wellness and social leadership, and closed with a collective resolve to make Bengaluru the world’s happiest city. Positioned as India’s first World Happpiness Summit, the day-long gathering was built around the idea that lasting happiness rests on three pillars: Pleasure, Peace and Purpose, the three Ps that give the brand its distinctive spelling. The morning session opened with the lighting of the lamp and an invocation, followed by Dr Kiran Bedi on the Fundamentals of Happiness and Arjun Kapoor on The Secret of Happiness. A panel on Success and Happiness brought together Govind Mahtani, Shareen, Nikhil Kamath and Hema Sardesai, while a second panel explored the Manifestation of Happiness through Attraction with Dr Amiett Kumar, Tarun Mishra, Rohit Khandelwal and Bhupendra Singh. Dr Saamdu Chetri, a pioneer of Bhutan’s Gross National Happiness philosophy, offered a global perspective on measuring wellbeing over wealth. The afternoon carried the momentum forward with Sonu Sharma on How to Be Happy Every Day and Aisshwarya DKS on The Science of Happiness. A panel on The Art of Being Happy featured Sruthi Hariharan, Preetika Rao, Archika Sudhanshu, Dr Aadhyaa Kumar and Renuka Goswami. Bringing the marquee sessions to a close, Shilpa Shetty spoke on The 3 Keys to Eternal Happiness, weaving together the wellness and positivity that have long defined her public life. Through the day, the summit also presented the Champion Awards, honouring individuals and organisations that foster positive work environments and champion the wellbeing of their people, extending the happiness conversation from the personal to the workplace.
